items.title: Architect, Barisal City Corporation
items.text: Early work on area development in a deltaic city, including the Bibir Pukur region and the Multipurpose City Market, later identified by the founder as the point at which he first felt the need for this approach.

items.title: Doctoral research on the early Buddhist architecture of Bengal
items.text: PhD in architectural history and theory, Nottingham Trent University. The founder describes this research as reinforcing his conviction that context shapes successful architecture.

items.title: Teaching at BRAC University
items.text: The founder joins BRAC University, where the philosophy is cultivated in design studios over the following decade.

items.title: First public workshop
items.text: ‘Exploring New Contextualism: An Approach to Architecture and Urban Design’, a lecture series and hands-on exercise at the School of Architecture and Design, BRAC University, Dhaka.

items.title: ‘A path to a sustainable and equitable future’
items.text: Essay setting out the approach's principles and origins, published in The Business Standard and by Arch-Bangla.

items.title: Workshop on New Contextualism 2.0
items.text: ‘Exploring New Contextualism 2.0: An Approach to Architecture and Urban Design’, Department of Architecture, BRAC University.

items.title: ‘An architectural philosophy for deltaic Bangladesh’
items.text: Essay in The Daily Star defining the ten dimensions as a ‘tenfold matrix’ and describing New Contextualism 2.0.

items.title: Online symposium
items.text: ‘Reflections on New Contextualism: Voices from Practice and Academia’, organised by the New Contextual Group.

items.title: ‘Architecture and Urbanism for People, Place, and Justice’
items.text: Essay by Reza and Nitu presenting five guiding principles, the ten-layer lens and a set of case studies.
